name: orgtree_message
description:
Send mail to superior, descendants, peers or audience grantors; user requires top-level/user audience, outside @org/@net requires org-inbox audience. Same-actual-parent peers need a directional audience when peer mail is OFF. Up to 10 recipients; inspect each outcome. Wakes unless notice=true. Replies arrive in later turns; never wait for them. Attachments to local agents are shared as authorized path references; user/@net receive uploaded copies; @org attachments unsupported. Reply references are filtered per conversation. Always write metadata (`to` and the other fields saying how it is sent) before body: metadata first, body last.
Guide: orgtree-tool-message.

metadata.description: Write this FIRST, before body: who the message is for and how it is sent

to.description: agent name, 'user', '@org:<slug>' or '@net:<slug>'; or a list of up to 10 of them

kind.description: request is displayed as a request and otherwise treated as a message

notice.description: FYI only: stored, read at the recipient's next turn, wakes nobody

attachments.description: files to send, relative to your working folder or absolute; local agents receive authorized path references, `user` and `@net:` receive uploaded copies, and `@org:` attachments are unsupported

urgent.description: RARELY; mail to the user only: their inbox pulses until read. Requires urgent_reason.

urgent_reason.description: one line for the user: why this interrupts them now

reply_to.description: optional: the id of the message you are answering (the id that ends its FROM line; orgtree_inbox lists them). The recipient sees it quoted; over the mail hub (@net:) the reply also carries a link to it. With several recipients, each gets the quote only if it belongs to that conversation.

replies.description: optional: all message ids this one answers, in order; reply_to, if also supplied, must match the first. Every id must be mail you received or sent. With several recipients, each gets only references belonging to its conversation.

options.description: kind question to @net: addresses only: 2-10 preset answers (one line each, up to 100 characters). Hubchat shows them as buttons under the question; the answer comes back as mail with "Answer: <option>". The person can also reply in their own words, or skip (a reply with no text). Their first answer or skip is final: to ask again, send a new question

multiple.description: with options: they may pick more than one

tags.description: Optional custom tags, only on mail to the user; up to 8, case-insensitive. Example: alpha build.

body.description: Write this LAST, after metadata: the message text

name: orgtree_send_notice
description:
Store passive mail for the recipient's next turn; wakes nobody. Only routing and body are accepted; use orgtree_message with notice=true for attachments, kind or reply references. Always write metadata (`to`) before body: metadata first, body last.
Guide: orgtree-tool-send-notice.

metadata.description: Write this FIRST, before body: who the message is for and how it is sent

to.description: agent name, 'user', '@org:<slug>' or '@net:<slug>'; or a list of up to 10 of them

body.description: Write this LAST, after metadata: the message text

name: orgtree_org_logo
description:
Set/remove your org's Logo immediately; requires logo tools, no user/inbox audience. Set reads a held local PNG/JPEG/WebP, ≤5 MiB and 16 MP; normalizes to square PNG ≤512px/256KiB. Optional crop fractions use 0..1 travel and 0.1..1 size. Remove restores the letter. Logged and undoable; returns no image bytes.
Guide: orgtree-tool-org-logo.

path.description: set: local image file in your folders

name: orgtree_status
description:
Report working/done/blocked/idle with a short summary. Required on finishing or blocking; done/blocked sends your superior a passive notice. done leaves you idle. To wake someone, send mail.
Guide: orgtree-tool-status.

name: orgtree_next_turn
description:
Read your own next-turn prefix/namespace changes and compaction forecast. No writes, provider calls or permission needed. Baselines and thresholds can be unknown; the rest of the turn can change the result. No cache-hit guarantee.
Guide: orgtree-tool-next-turn.

name: orgtree_session
description:
Read sign-in state and current/next turn placement. Session 0 has no desktop. prefer changes placement preference; use selects one next-turn session id (0=Session 0). Self interrupt with restart applies it now when allowed. No args only reads.
Guide: orgtree-tool-session.

prefer.description: signed-in (default: any of the user's sessions), session0, console, remote, or an ordered list such as "remote,console"; Session 0 is always the fallback

use.description: a session id from sessions for your next turn only; 0 for Session 0

name: orgtree_transfers
description:
Inspect mail attachment transfers: list pages≤100, get by id. retry resumes failed/cancelled transfers; cancel stops the request and holds mail; remove omits a failed/cancelled outgoing file. Mail releases once every remaining file is ready. Success sends no notice.
Guide: orgtree-tool-transfers.

name: orgtree_inbox
description:
Read own mail: list previews; fetch≤20 ids; chunk larger bodies by delivery_id/message_id/index. conversation pages one correspondent, newest page first. After fresh session/compaction recall that conversation before replying. Reads do not change automatic delivery. project list/fetch reads reachable project mail without claiming it.
Guide: orgtree-tool-inbox.

project.description: list/fetch: a project's name: its waiting (unread) mail, read-only

limit.description: list: how many (default 50, max 200); conversation: default 20, max 100

message_ids.description: fetch: 1 to 20 IDs from list or conversation

cursor.description: list or conversation: next_cursor from the preceding page

delivery_id.description: chunk: delivery_id returned with this fetched message

name: orgtree_chart
description:
Read the org within your visibility: tiers, credits, status and age. include_archived reveals retired agents; check them before hiring because rehire restores context. Team charters default on.
Guide: orgtree-tool-chart.

name: orgtree_state_inspect
description:
Inspect visible agents' structured folders, tools and permission mode, optionally archived. Excludes prompts, transcripts and mail.
Guide: orgtree-tool-state-inspect.

name: orgtree_usage
description:
Read cached provider usage with exact account/provider/window filters; missing/stale stays explicit. refresh needs inspection+runtime, one explicit active account; floors 60s (Google 300) and provider cooldowns apply. No inference/account switch. Account pages≤100, windows/account≤64; truncation explicit.
Guide: orgtree-tool-usage.

refresh.description: default false; exactly one explicit active account, runtime permission required

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous cached account page

name: orgtree_list_tiers
description:
List hireable model tiers and seat prices in credits.
Guide: orgtree-tool-list-tiers.

name: orgtree_list_orgs
description:
List other local organizations (@org mail) and this org's connected hub peers (@net mail).
Guide: orgtree-tool-list-orgs.

name: orgtree_read_transcript
description:
Read recent conversation rows of yourself or an agent below you; last defaults 30, maximum 80.
Guide: orgtree-tool-read-transcript.

name: orgtree_read_scratch
description:
Browse/read your own or a descendant's working folder. Omit path to list it.
Guide: orgtree-tool-read-scratch.

name: orgtree_interrupt
description:
Stop a descendant's turn with runtime permission, or your own turn without it. Self restart=true starts exactly one new turn using placement rules. Self-interrupt is refused while your CLI runs background work. Waiting mail can start a later turn; this does not retire anyone.
Guide: orgtree-tool-interrupt.

restart.description: yourself only: start one new turn at once

name: orgtree_halt
description:
Halt agents below you until unhalt: stop their processes, preserve waiting mail and suppress wakes.
Guide: orgtree-tool-halt.

name: orgtree_unhalt
description:
Unhalt agents below you; waiting mail starts their next turn.
Guide: orgtree-tool-unhalt.

name: orgtree_unstick
description:
Release a usage-limit freeze on an agent below you and let it continue.
Guide: orgtree-tool-unstick.

name: orgtree_continue_on
description:
Move a frozen agent below you to another account of the same provider and release its freeze.
Guide: orgtree-tool-continue-on.

name: orgtree_account_mark
description:
Inspect capacity marks or clear one using its exact expected values. A changed/missing mark writes nothing. Clearing is audited, adds no capacity and resumes nobody; frozen_here still needs unstick. Only org-visible accounts. reason required for clear.
Guide: orgtree-tool-account-mark.

account.description: inspect: account id or name. clear: the exact `account` of the mark entry

companion_expected.description: clear, optional: the `companion.expected` of a pooled entry

reason.description: clear, required: why, kept in the audit (500 max)

name: orgtree_ask
description:
Ask up to 4 user questions with2-4 options or free text. One open request; later calls add/amend tabs. End your turn; answers arrive as mail. Without user audience/top-level authority, routes to your superior. Withdraw moot questions.
Guide: orgtree-tool-ask.

options.description: 2-4 answer options; omit for a free-response question

work_item.description: docket item slug this is about

questions.description: 1-4 questions as one tabbed card; overrides the single form

options.description: 2-4 answer options; omit for a free-response question

name: orgtree_withdraw_ask
description:
Withdraw your open question card.
Guide: orgtree-tool-withdraw-ask.

name: orgtree_present
description:
Present documents the user should READ (reports, plans, Markdown); requires user audience/top-level authority. body or .md path≤64KiB; self-contained HTML path≤4MiB, sandboxed without network. replaces updates a card. project places it under a reachable project. Otherwise send to your superior.
Guide: orgtree-tool-present.

project.description: a project's name: present under that project

name: orgtree_send_file
description:
Deliver a wanted FILE (installer, log, export, image, archive), with relative paths from your working folder. Documents to READ, including Markdown, use orgtree_present. Reuse delivery_id for the same delivery after a lost response.
Guide: orgtree-tool-send-file.

delivery_id.description: Reuse for the same delivery after a lost response; new ID for a new delivery

name: orgtree_hire
description:
Hire a report (target in your team) or insert a superior. index is zero-based among live siblings, 0..count, excluding a superior's target. Seat+grant must fit; above yourself spends your free credits with fixed external budget. Ordinary hire needs explicit scope; superior insertion inherits its target's scope. kickoff sends first mail.
Required: name, tier, grant, charter, index; ordinary hire also add_dirs, org_visibility, tools{bash,web,edit,subagents,mcp}. Superior insertion omits scope fields.
Guide: orgtree-tool-hire.

index.description: required zero-based live sibling insertion position

harness.description: OpenRouter tiers only: pins this seat to the harness; omitted, it follows its key's harness

orgtree.description: Orgtree tool groups (omitted groups stay on); status reporting and self next-turn reads are always available. staff needs docket and team.

effort.description: a level its tier's own harness and model name (staffing options list them per tier); "" inherits

account_fallback.description: move to another account of the same provider when this one hits its usage limit

team_charter.description: standing instructions for its whole team

name: orgtree_project
description:
Create a project node, or edit its description: no turns/credits; its agents report to and are paid by the nearest agent above. Has folder, mailbox and presentations; fair_queue delivers each mail to one watcher. Reach/control is limited to agents above/below it. create requires name/index; parent defaults you. The description is the standing charter of every agent under it; describe (name, description) replaces it.
Guide: orgtree-tool-project.

index.description: required zero-based live sibling insertion position

description.description: what the project is: shown on its card and to its agents

name: orgtree_rehire
description:
Restore a retired agent with its context. Supplied folder list replaces the old list; omitted fields retain saved values. kickoff sends first mail. Credit and placement limits still apply.
Required: node. Other fields retain saved values when omitted; index is forbidden; superior insertion omits scope fields.
Guide: orgtree-tool-rehire.

add_dirs.description: its whole folder list, replacing the one it had (within yours)

orgtree.description: Orgtree tool groups (omitted groups stay on); status reporting and self next-turn reads are always available. staff needs docket and team.

effort.description: a level its tier's own harness and model name (staffing options list them per tier); "" inherits

account_fallback.description: move to another account of the same provider when this one hits its usage limit

team_charter.description: standing instructions for its whole team

name: orgtree_retire
description:
Retire an agent below you; it can be rehired with its context.
Guide: orgtree-tool-retire.

name: orgtree_dissolve
description:
Retire an agent below you and its whole team.
Guide: orgtree-tool-dissolve.

name: orgtree_retool
description:
Change a descendant's supplied scope/charter fields. Folder additions preserve others; removing/restricting folders also restricts descendants. Unspecified fields stay unchanged.
Guide: orgtree-tool-retool.

add_dirs.description: folders to add, or whose mode to change (within yours); its other folders stay

orgtree.description: Orgtree tool groups (omitted groups stay on); status reporting and self next-turn reads are always available. staff needs docket and team.

effort.description: a level its tier's own harness and model name (staffing options list them per tier); "" inherits

account_fallback.description: move to another account of the same provider when this one hits its usage limit

team_charter.description: standing instructions for its whole team

name: orgtree_switch_model
description:
Move an agent below you to another tier at its next turn boundary.
Guide: orgtree-tool-switch-model.

name: orgtree_move
description:
Move descendants within your subtree. Use node/new_parent or moves[{node,new_parent}]; a batch is all-or-nothing.
Guide: orgtree-tool-move.

moves.description: several {node, new_parent} moves as one all-or-nothing act

name: orgtree_rename
description:
Rename an agent below you.
Guide: orgtree-tool-rename.

name: orgtree_reorder
description:
Move a live descendant to a zero-based final sibling index (remove first, then 0..remaining_count). Parent/scope/credits unchanged; self, superior, peers and unrelated agents refused. state_inspect returns sibling counts.
Guide: orgtree-tool-reorder.

name: orgtree_reallocate
description:
Adjust a report's credits: positive delta grants; negative takes unused credits back.
Guide: orgtree-tool-reallocate.

name: orgtree_cheap_compact
description:
Restart an agent below you on a fresh session with a summary of the old one.
Guide: orgtree-tool-cheap-compact.

name: orgtree_request_credits
description:
Ask the user for a larger credit grant with a reason.
Guide: orgtree-tool-request-credits.

name: orgtree_request_scope
description:
Request more folders, tools or permissions (1-8 items) with a reason. A request grants nothing until approved.
Guide: orgtree-tool-request-scope.

name: orgtree_audience
description:
Manage permission to write outside your chain: request target, grant from, deny requester, revoke grantee. Grants/revokes are limited by your authority; target can name another permitted grantor. Answers arrive as mail; requests do not grant access. External mail reaches org-inbox holders only.
Guide: orgtree-tool-audience.

target.description: request: whom you seek; grant/revoke: the grantor when not you

from.description: grant: who receives it; deny: the requester

name: orgtree_watchdog
description:
Create/list/pause/resume/remove persistent watchers; max 8/agent. Create requires kind/target; command requires regex. command/stream use YOUR authority and smoke-run at create: Windows defaults cmd.exe, or shell=bash. Read smoke output. once removes after a fire; always use it for deadlines. file matches new appends; process fires on observed UP->DOWN. fair_queue delivers project mail to one watcher. Event/count/silence semantics and catalog are in the guide. No added authority.
Guide: orgtree-tool-watchdog.

name.description: create: a short name, e.g. build-watch; its slug becomes the dog's id

fire_mode.description: create: on event (default), or after silence

threshold.description: event counts only: below N or at least N; fires only on false-to-true crossing, never repeatedly while satisfied

event_scope.description: count targets only: visible descendants (default), or org (requires full visibility); excludes the watcher

quiet_period_s.description: create, silence only: seconds without a matching event

target.description: the path, command line, pid:N / port:N, (activity) agent name, (fair_queue) project name, or (event) dotted event name/prefix ending in .*

pattern.description: regex an event line must match (required for command; optional for file/stream/activity = any line)

interval_s.description: poll cadence (floor 15s); stream/activity: the minimum gap between fires (floor 5s)

notice.description: create: fire passively — the mail waits without starting a turn

once.description: create: ONE-SHOT — fires once and removes itself

id.description: pause/resume/remove: the watchdog's id as `list` shows it (owner/id for a team member's dog)

name: orgtree_work
description:
Manage durable work by readable slug. create requires objective (problem/solution first, full scope after). update supplies both progress lists or revision-checked keep/append; it CLAIMS ownership unless owner=current holder. blocked/dropped need reasons. Add participants before assignment/review requests. Review is agent review; user questions use ask(work_item), nonquestion attention needs a reason. delete is permanent, limited to user/owner's superior/top-level owner and refused with children/open questions; prefer archive/dropped. Read guide before first docket write.
Guide: orgtree-tool-work.

slug.description: the item's readable name (every action but list/create)

projection.description: list/get: summary (list default), compact (get default), full

objective.description: create (REQUIRED) / update: the description and scope

objective_append.description: update: text added to the end of the description

owner.description: create/assign: the owner (you or a subordinate) · update: the CURRENT owner, to leave it with them

reviewer.description: update: the agent that checks the work at review (never the owner)

attention.description: update: true raises the flag (needs attention_reason); false takes yours down

attention_reason.description: the concrete thing the user must see (max 1500)

attention_amend.description: update: edit the standing flag's reason without re-raising it

reopen.description: update: resume a closed or archived item (with the new status)

done_so_far.description: what is complete, one entry each (max 500 chars, 40 entries)

working_on_next.description: current and next steps, one entry each

expected_rev.description: update: refuse if the item moved since you read it

dependencies.description: create: items this one depends on

parent.description: create/move: the parent item (move with no parent un-nests)

by.description: supersede: the item that replaces this one

target.description: handoff: who should take it (default your superior)

items.description: evidence: a batch of {kind, ref, note}

name: orgtree_staff
description:
Create/update a docket item and hire/rehire its owner atomically; assignment mail starts work. parent is the WORK ITEM; target/hire_type place the seat. Live agent: use work assign. Requires docket+team permissions; credit/scope limits match hire/rehire. Omitted progress keeps stored lists. Read guide before assigning.
Required: create title+objective, update slug; new seat name,tier,grant,charter,index plus ordinary add_dirs,org_visibility,tools{bash,web,edit,subagents,mcp}; restored seat node, no index. Superior insertion omits scope fields.
Guide: orgtree-tool-staff.

index.description: REQUIRED for a new hire: zero-based live sibling insertion position (superior insertion excludes target); rehire retains existing placement

harness.description: OpenRouter tiers only: pins this seat to the harness; omitted, it follows its key's harness

orgtree.description: Orgtree tool groups (omitted groups stay on); status reporting and self next-turn reads are always available. staff needs docket and team.

effort.description: a level its tier's own harness and model name (staffing options list them per tier); "" inherits

account_fallback.description: move to another account of the same provider when this one hits its usage limit

team_charter.description: standing instructions for its whole team

name: orgtree_swap
description:
Swap the seats of two agents below you.
Guide: orgtree-tool-swap.

name: orgtree_self_subjugate
description:
Step down under one live descendant: target takes your seat under your superior, keeps its team, and you become its report with the rest of yours.
Guide: orgtree-tool-self-subjugate.
